root.name: Grünfeld Defense: Flohr Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Nf3 Bg7 5. Qa4+

overview: 5.Qa4+ is a sidestep in the Three Knights Grünfeld: White checks to take the sting out of ...dxc4 and keeps the centre. After 5...Bd7 6.Qb3 dxc4 7.Qxc4 O-O (or 5...c6) Black has given up the centre but has an easy game with ...Nc6 or ...c5 breaks. White gets a space advantage but the queen can be harassed.

white_ideas.idea: Build a central pawn pair with e4 and keep the queen safe
Complete development with Bg5 or e3 and O-O

typical_structures.structure: Grünfeld with White centre pawns on d4/e4 and the Black fianchetto bishop on g7

character.notes: A queen check and a quiet continuation make it less forcing than the main Grünfeld.

gambit.notes: Any pawn on c4 is regained by the queen, so no gambit.

structure.notes: Centre under tension, with d4 attacked by ...c5.

approach.notes: Less common than 4.Bf4 or the Exchange but respected.

level.notes: Plans are clear for both sides, though Grünfeld middlegames need understanding.

character.reason: A quieter Grünfeld sideline with no early forcing play.

gambit.reason: Any pawn taken on c4 comes back by force.

structure.reason: The centre is under tension and could go several ways.

level.reason: It asks for understanding of Grünfeld plans more than long theory.

plans.reason: Black lets White build a centre and attacks it with the g7 bishop and ...c5.
